items.title: Splitting fields of finite abelian induced torsors over iterated Laurent series control toral quotients
items.author: Danny Ofek; Zinovy Reichstein; Federico Scavia
items.difficulty_reason: The complete two-part main theorem connects finite splitting degrees and Galois groups over iterated Laurent series to toral quotients inside arbitrary algebraic groups. Its proof reconstructs tame finite images, uses rank-r henselian valuation rings and equivariant properness of a Borel quotient to detect torality, then controls restriction indices and prime-to-characteristic Galois quotient/subgroup structure. Original connected torsor, algebraically closed ground field, prime-to-characteristic order and tower assumptions retained. Old torsion-index preliminaries are support, not the splitting-field theorem.

primary.label: Complete original two-part main torsor splitting theorem

proof_spans.label: Complete original group/Laurent-Galois prerequisites, valuation/Borel torality proof and both splitting-field conclusions

contexts.label: Original toral and torsion-index definitions and applications setup
Original applications and adjacent main results retained uncounted
